dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I don't much like spending time in places where there's nothing to do. It's like looking at a blank page in a book.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But since you're here, maybe we can liven things up a little to make this time more meaningful.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Like... Ooh, we could share some stories with each other before we set off again.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I'm really curious to know what's at the end of this maze, too.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: And yes, I know that as we go further in, we're bound to meet tougher and tougher monsters, and maybe even suffer some setbacks along the way.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But after the winds and rain have passed, the saplings in the forest grow a little bigger and a little stronger. We'll only get to see the blue sky above the treetops if we keep pressing on, right?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Children have all sorts of wonderful dreams, with more colors than even the feathers of the Dusk Bird.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But once they grow up, their once-vibrant dreams slowly begin to fade.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Luckily, we can use the written word to make a record of our dreams before they disappear. Maybe, when it comes down to it, that's what fairytales are.
